source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; footnote reports the Perugio Latin variant; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: The Number of Prorogators, and also the Part of Fortune — footnote 144 callout and endnote
source_locator.short_quote: if the Moon should so follow the Sun ... according to the succession of the signs ... if the Moon precede the Sun ... contrary to the succession

prerequisites: relative order of the Sun and Moon
calculation_dependencies: relative order of the Sun and Moon

relative_order.Moon_follows_Sun: count from the Ascendant according to the succession of the signs
relative_order.Moon_precedes_Sun: count from the Ascendant contrary to the succession of the signs

normalized_rule: Under the Perugio Latin variant reported in Ashmand's footnote, use the Sun-Moon degree interval from the main text and count from the Ascendant in the direction of the signs when the Moon follows the Sun and in the opposite direction when the Moon precedes the Sun.
synthesis_notes: This is a transmitted directional restatement in an editorial footnote, not an independently established competing calculation or default.
review_notes: Retain the Perugio footnote restatement without selecting a winner. It uses the Sun-Moon degree interval stated in the main text but supplies directional wording reported in the footnote; it is linked to the main-text candidate through an open transmission-review record, not asserted as a proven chart-changing fork.
transmission_notes: This procedure appears as an additional passage in the 1646 Perugio Latin translation reported in Ashmand's footnote 144; it is not stated in the same form in Ashmand's main text. The same footnote says the related Cardan formulation is exactly equivalent, so the cited edition does not establish a chart-changing computational fork. Certainty is disputed as a Ptolemaic/main-text reading and is limited to the cited transmission.
